The week I spend in New York for #Goalkeepers2030 and the UN General Assembly is always a highlight of my year. Last week was no exception.
At #Goalkeepers2030, I spoke with Archbishop Vicenzo Paglia about how people and relationships must remain at the center of how we use AI.

We have an opportunity—and an obligation—to ensure that AI tools are designed to improve lives and reach the people who stand to benefit most, including farmers, teachers, and health workers.  

Progress doesn’t happen on its own. It happens because the world invests in and prioritizes it. If we can combine increased generosity with the smart use of AI, there’s no limit to the progress we can make.

There are around 7,000 languages spoken worldwide, yet most AI tools are still built primarily in English. The Gates Foundation is joining a coalition of organizations to help nearly 3.4 billion people whose languages are underrepresented in AI. Over the next five years, these services will provide access to them in their own language and voice. #goalkeepers2030
I’m excited to be in New York this week to keep the conversation around AI moving forward and to build on the incredible progress we’re making. #Goalkeepers2030
Seth Rogen and Lauren Miller Rogen founded Hilarity for Charity to make sure no one has to care for a loved one with Alzheimer’s alone.

AI could be a great equalizer, but only if it’s built to benefit the people who need it most. 

That’s why the Gates Foundation is committing $1 billion over the next two years to expand access to AI and the solutions, opportunities, and knowledge that are too often inaccessible for many around the world—in health clinics, in classrooms, and on farms. 

This year’s Goalkeepers Report focuses on the urgent actions needed to ensure AI narrows the gaps between the richest and poorest rather than widening them.

AI gives us a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help more solutions reach the people who need them. But there are three things the world needs to get right first. Explore more in the 2026 Goalkeepers Report.
AI has huge potential for agriculture, especially in low-income countries—and Neema Mduma is helping lead the way with KilimoAI.

Did you know that @Virgin once imagined the iPod, but we made it into an April Fool’s joke!

In 1986, we announced the Virgin Music Box: a machine that could store music and let you call up any song you wanted. We thought it was so farfetched it would pass as a ‘gotcha’ moment. How wrong we were!

Years later, the world caught up with the idea, and I remember thinking: we should have built the bloody thing. The moral of the story is that when an idea feels slightly ridiculous, don’t dismiss it too quickly.

You have to make every one of your employees and team members understand that you care about them more than you want them to care about you. I know that sounds impossible, but you can’t be crippled by the task. It’s tough. But, if you do it, you will build a great culture. If you do not, every day that you work will take you further and further away from that culture. You have to practice this everyday. It means not being afraid to fire your top salesperson because they’re also not a nice person…it means knowing who your employees are, what drives them, and if their needs have changed. It also means promoting and compensating people based on how hard they work, not on how well you know them. A great work culture is one that “works” for everyone. It should work when things are easy and it should work when, God forbid, tragedy occurs. The second you slack on your culture is the second you lose. Today is World Mental Health Day. And we’ve made great progress in recent years raising awareness and opening up the conversation about mental health.

This year, I hope we take it one step further: mental health is brain health. A growing body of research shows how our brain health connects to everything from daily brain fog and anxiety to long-term cognitive decline.

The last time we sat down, I was warned that a tsunami of change was coming. Now he's back, and he believes we're starting to see it unfold. This is Eric Weinstein, a Harvard-trained mathematician and physicist who's spent decades challenging conventional ideas about the universe. What I find interesting about Eric is how he connects subjects like physics, technology, politics and history to make sense of what's happening in the world. And with everything going on right now, I wanted to understand what concerns him most and what he thinks we might be missing. We discussed things like: - Why he believes the world has just woken up from an 80-year sleep. - His concerns about Iran, Russia and the possibility of nuclear war. - Why China is watching what's happening in the West. - How AI could change the future of science and work. - His theories about UFOs and government secrecy. - Why he believes humanity may need to leave our solar system. At one point, Eric suggests America could be approaching its own version of the Suez Crisis, when Britain was forced to confront how much global power it had lost. captions: Rather than buying things for less than their worth, make your brand so strong that when you buy something, it becomes more valuable by its association to you.

Pricing is the single strongest lever on profit in a business.

And yet - 95% of business owners look at what everyone else is charging, take the average, make that their price and never think about it again.

The problem is - the business owners they’re copying are broke too.

You want to sleep at night like you know everything is gonna work out.

And you want to wake up like there’s no chance it’ll happen unless you take relentless, unyielding, like-your-life-depends-on-it action.

If you’re not making money, it’s because:

You don’t know how to solve a valuable problem.
Or 
You can but no one knows about you.

That’s it.

Rule of life:

Never make asks of someone bigger than you. Give until they offer.

Simplest path to making money:

1) Find a service people already buy
2) Do it in half the time, make it twice as easy for the customer, or remove all risk
3) Ask everyone you know if they know anybody who wants it
4) Charge more than everyone else
5) Dont stop when u get bored

Find what works.
Do more of what works.
Find the thing preventing you from doing more of what works.
Solve it.
Do more of what works.
Repeat.

When things get hard, here’s a phrase I like to tell myself:

“This is for now, not forever.”

No matter what the scoreboard says, you always win when you leave it all on the field.

When you finish with nothing left to give.

A hill I will die on:

Your spouse is either your biggest asset or biggest liability.
There is no inbetween.
Choose wisely.

Sanchez shared this You will NEVER win in business without the 3 R’s - Referrals, Recurring Revenue, and REVIEWS. 1) Referrals Make it easy for people to tell their friends. Give excellent service, then ask if anyone else could benefit. Create a referral program, hold a contest, and do everything in your power to get your customers talking about you. Because do you know what your best customer has that you need? Friends who are more likely to give you business if they tell them about you. 2) Recurring Revenue This isn’t me telling you to slap a subscription model over your tree-cutting business. At least, not exactly… Recurring rev is predictable revenue. It's much easier it is to project cashflow when you KNOW a certain amount revenue is already accounted for. Plus, your LTV will increase exponentially when you create a recurring revenue stream. Figure out how to sell packages that renew every month, quarter, or year. Sell packages, offer bulk discounts, and otherwise set up a system that makes it easy for someone to “set it and forget it.” 3) Referrals I know its uncomfortable to ask but MAN is it important. Help people say nice things about you, by asking for a review post-purchase. Expect 1-5% of people to say, “dont ask me again,” and get used to rejection. I know most of you have never owned a business, but THIS is the core of what business owners need to do. People don’t blindly trust anymore, so they need to see others like them loving you. If you aren't already reaching out at least 1x a day to ask for a review from a happy customer, you will be amazed by the ROI. This is the OWNER MINDSET. Ready to get in the owner game?
